steps.text: Place butter in a shallow bowl and set aside until needed for kneading.
Place marshmallows in a large microwave-safe bowl and microwave on high to start melting the marshmallows, 30 seconds to 1 minute.
Carefully stir water and vanilla into hot marshmallows; stir until the mixture is smooth.
Slowly beat in confectioners' sugar, 1 cup at a time, until you have a sticky dough. Reserve 1 cup confectioners' sugar for kneading. The dough will be very stiff.

Rub your hands thoroughly with butter and begin kneading the sticky dough. As you knead, the dough will become workable and pliable. Turn the dough out onto a working surface dusted with confectioners' sugar and continue kneading until the fondant is smooth and no longer sticky to the touch, 5 to 10 minutes.
Form the fondant into a ball, wrap it tightly in plastic wrap, and refrigerate, 8 hours to overnight.
To use, allow the fondant to come to room temperature and roll it out onto a flat surface dusted with confectioners' sugar.

raw_recipe.headline: Marshmallow Fondant
raw_recipe.description: Marshmallow fondant made with mini marshmallows. This sweet, tasty, and fun rolled fondant is much easier to make than a traditional boiled fondant.

review.reviewBody: I made this with MARSHMALLOW FLUFF!!!! I definitely recommend to do it this way! Based on the previous reviews of saying to wait till the melted marshmallows cooled, I skipped the melting the marshmallows and water step and I placed a whole container of marshmallow fluff into the refrigerator over night. The next morning, I sprayed my kitchen aid very well with PAM, dumped the whole container of Marshmallow fluff into the KA and food coloring and confectioner/powdered sugar as needed. This really was not that difficult or messy at all. When the fondant was at a good consistency, I placed it into plastic wrap and into the freezer for about a 1/2 hour. I then rolled it out and it rolled really nicely. I used this fondant to cover a barbie doll cake than I made for my daughter's birthday! I spread a very thin layer of regular frosting onto the cakes surface to make sure the fondant would stick to the cake. It came out great!

I made this recipe today for my first attempt with fondant. I made the fondant in my kitchenaid mixer because I didn't want to kneed the dough for 10 minutes. Kitchenaids have that great attachment just for that! So, I made the fondant, colored it in 2 different colors, and all went well... until I rolled it out. I used powdered sugar on a silicone mat, kind of like flour for bread dough. This stuff stuck like nothing else. I didn't know anything would stick to silicone mats, but this stuff did. I added more powdered sugar, and it stuck. So, I had a mess of a time. Until I figured out that the author had specified that you use butter to kneed the dough to keep it from sticking to your hands. I hadn't added any butter, because I wasn't kneeding it by hand. I added a little butter, and sure enough, the stuff rolled out like a dream. It didn't stick, it was easy to handle, and everything went smooth from there. I am so pleased with this recipe! I will for sure make it again, I had so much fun making this cake! Next time, I will have the kitchenaid do the kneeding again, but I will add the 1/4 cup butter to the mix. Thank you, I love it!

I've never made fondant and I was not too keen on the traditional version with glycerin and unflavored gelatin - "specialty items". This one had such simple ingredients! Couple of tips: grease your hands frequently (I used Crisco), even if your hands are covered with goo. It helps it come off your hands, so don't panic as I nearly did! I divided it in half to knead and realized that the batch that sat for a while was a lot easier to work with, so next time I'll let it "rest" before kneading. Last, I used my Kitchen Aid with the dough hook to mix and it worked great.

I only made was halving the recipe, which was more than enough for the cake I did. I also used my Kitchen Aid to mix the initial stages. I also had to periodically stop, empty the mixer bowl and regrease. The taste is great, not plastic like bought fondant. The texture is nice and smooth. The only recommendation that I would suggest is, like others, use Crisco to grease EVERYTHING!

Fantastic Fondant. I make mine using my Kitchenaid, so much easier. Melt the marshmallows and water together, put that into your Kitchenaid bowl with the knead nook, add the vanilla, and then slowly incorporate the powdered sugar. When it is almost fulling incorporated, roll onto a heavy powdered countertop and knead by hand, adding additional sugar until smooth. No Butter Needed! I make at least 1 cake a week using this method and it turns out perfect!

I have been procrastinating for years. Had I known it was this easy to make fondant, we'll, let's just say I'm kicking myself.
 I needed small batches of fondant in 7 different colors, so I had to break down the recipe a little and I shaved off some kneading time, which is nice.
 To get 1 disk of fondant, approximately 1/2 cup in size, I did the following...
 In a microwaveable 1 qt bowl, microwave 1 cup of mini Marshmallows for exactly 30 seconds. Stir until smooth, about 20 seconds. Add 1 1/4 top water, 1/8 top clear vanilla extract, food coloring gel. Stir until it gets difficult to stir, then grease your hands with Crisco and, using hands, scrape out dough onto Powdered sugar-dusted counter. Knead dough about 2-3 minutes until smooth and glossy, reapplying Crisco to hands as needed, and generously dusting counter with more PS as needed.
 Form into disc and seal in small plastic zip-top bag. Chill in fridge overnight.
 I am giving the recipe, as written, 5 stars. Fabulous. 
 The recipe, with my revisions, is also worth 5 stars! 
 Hope this helps. Happy baking!

If the marshmallows aren't totally melted, just add the water, vanilla and the powered sugar, one cup at a time. After you get more than half the powdered sugar, let a kitchen aid take care of the rest of the kneading. This will also cut down on the butter/crisco. When you roll out the fondant, use extra powdered sugar and keep checking the board for stickiness; especially if you are rolling out large sheets of fondant.

This was the first time I made my own fondant. It tastes far better than store bought pre-made. I divided it into three parts. One large plain white part and one small orange dyed part and one larger purple part and one good size pink part. I have put it in the frig and will take it out again in a day or two to make the flowers, calla lillies, fantasy flowers, and plumeria flowers for my daughter's 6th birthday cake. It will be gorgeous and this fondant recipe was awesome. It was easy to make too. I do not own a microwave, but I put my marshmallows in my mixer bowl over a pot of boiling water and the marshmallows melted perfectly! I do not recommend kneading this in your mixer if you have a Hamilton Beach stand mixer. It tried to kill it, so I did the rest of the kneading on my counter. It worked fine. Plus my kids got to play with some too, so we all had some fun this morning. Thanks so much for the recipe!!

Easy and awesome! Might be a bit of an upper body workout if you don't have a Kitchen Aid. Second time using fondant. This soft and pliable fondant rolled out very easily. Paste coloring worked better than the liquid. Had to add more powdered sugar to the red parts because the drops made it sticky. Made a batch of white, then kneaded in colors as I went. Not sure if this would dry and stiffen for flowers though. I did not chill it.

This was excellent and easy! It did take longer than a minute to get the marshmallows to melt enough. I put it in as it said and put the water and vanilla, but after stirring it wasn't smooth enough so I put it back again for maybe 20 seconds? Then stirred again and repeated until it wasn't lumpy anymore. I used shortening (generic Crisco) instead of butter as someone mentioned and it turned out great! Everything else I followed the recipe! Once the stickiness went away (the shortening definitely helped with this! Keep recoating your hands with it!) it was very pliable. It made a lot too. I was able to completely cover the cake once with one color (the cake was 9-inch diameter, 2 layers tall) and make several decorations for the top, and I still had a LOT left over. I probably could've covered the cake a few more times with all the fondant it made! Before laying the fondant, I did cut the rounded tops off each layer of cake so it'd be flat. I completely iced the yellow cake in chocolate frosting, and then I laid the fondant. Believe it or not the combination of the traditional yellow/chocolate cake with the marshmallow fondant actually worked really well! Before refrigerating, I divided the fondant and colored each as needed before wrapping up. It didn't take long to bring it back to room temperature (I even warmed it up a bit with my hands right when I took it out, before unwrapping it). I got a lot of compliments on the appearance and the taste of this cake! It was a lot of

I made fondant for the first time using this recipe and was surprised how well it turned out. I added my food coloring after I stired in the water and doubled the vanilla. I lost count of how much powdered sugar I used, it mm ay have been about a cup more then the recipe, you just keep adding more till its the correct consistancy. After the fondant was no longer sticky, I wrapped it up and put it in the refrigerator for a couple house (I didn't plan ahead to have it sit over night). I warmed up the fondant in the microwave on a low level till it was workable but not warm. It was easy to roll out and was pleased with the results and it tasted great.

This is my go to recipe for fondant cakes. I was told i couldn't make a black fondant and would have to airbrush the cake to achieve what i was looking for, but I got a very nice and dark black color by starting with brown and orange marshmallows and adding my black gel coloring

This was amazing. My granddaughter wanted a Rainbow birthday cake. Made a beautiful rainbow for the top. After reading some reviews about how sticky it was I sprayed the glass bowl I used to melt the marshmallows with canola oil. No sticking. I then dumped them into the stainless steel bowl of my kitchenaid mixer which I also sprayed with canola as well as the paddle beater. Great consistency right away. Was no need to refrigerate first. My rainbow is on wax paper on a baking tray which I slid into a 2 gallon Ziplock bag. Putting it on the cake in a few days. I sprayed my hands and rolling pin too. No sticking.
Brain cake my grandson made for a science class.
16oz marshmallow to 2lbs of confectioners sugar is not enough. It took me almost 4 lbs of sugar to get it to the proper consistency. It tastes good but this is a bad recipe it's incorrect.

I love this recipe! You couldn't go wrong with having a video of how to make it. The fondant came out very smooth and tasty! I did add a twp of almond extract and some without. Tasted great and easy to work with. I didn't even have to have it out very long before using. Thank you!
It worked awesome! Just don't skip chilling it. :D Thank you!
It was way too sweet----and we didn't even put all the sugar it called for. It got as hard as a rock overnight.

So far so good! Made it no time at all! If you are afraid to get your hands dirty I recommend you buy it lol, or at the very least use a pasrty hook. You will have to kneed it though! It tastes good! It is chilling right now. The only I changed was I used Crisco instead of butter on my hands! Will update tomorrow if any issues but judging by how it has come out so far, this is a hit. Texture is great! As long as it rolls out we are good. I am going to try adding color next time too!
Nice fondant, tastes good and can usually create anything 3D.
